title: Script development and invocation
subtitle: Sha-bang, interpreters, and how you run a script

cards.meaning: A list of system commands stored in a file
cards.example: commands you would type, saved in a file
cards.notes: Saves retyping that sequence each time. Memory hook: a script = commands you would type, saved so you do not type them again.

cards.front: How the shell runs a script
cards.meaning: Interprets the file line by line (not compiling a binary)
cards.example: bash reads each line and runs it
cards.notes: Same idea as interactive shell use — the file is fed to an interpreter.

cards.meaning: At the head of a script: tells the system which command interpreter gets the file
cards.notes: Course spelling is sha-bang (same idea as shebang). Must be the first line. Kernel reads those two characters, then the path.

cards.meaning: Path to the program that interprets the script (shell, language, or utility)
cards.notes: Optional arguments may follow the path (e.g. -f for sed/awk). Prefer an absolute interpreter, or env + a name on PATH.

cards.meaning: Bourne / POSIX sh interprets the file
cards.notes: First line of the script when you want sh.
First line when you want Bash features.
Shows sha-bang can name a programming language, not only a shell.

cards.meaning: Run python found on PATH (env locates it)
cards.notes: Used when python is not always at one fixed path (pyenv, /usr/bin/python3, …). env searches PATH and execs the first python.

cards.meaning: sed interprets the file; -f = take the rest of the file as the program
cards.notes: Optional argument after the interpreter path.

cards.meaning: awk interprets the file; -f = file is the awk program
cards.notes: Same idea as sed -f: the script body is the program.

cards.meaning: Often still works on Linux (kernel may fall back to /bin/sh) — do not rely on that
cards.notes: Put the sha-bang line in. Do not depend on the fallback.

cards.meaning: Run the file with sh; execute bit not required
cards.notes: You pick the interpreter. Sha-bang is ignored in the sense that you already chose sh — even if #! says something else.

cards.meaning: Run the file with bash; execute bit not required
cards.notes: Same pattern as sh scriptname: named shell is the interpreter regardless of sha-bang.
Needed before ./scriptname so the kernel can treat the file as a program.

cards.meaning: Run an executable script; kernel uses the sha-bang interpreter
cards.notes: Execute bit required. Who interprets = path after #!.

cards.meaning: ./ is required when the directory is not on PATH (current directory usually is not)
cards.notes: Without ./ (or another path), the shell looks up the name on PATH and will not find a file only in .

cards.meaning: sh/bash file: no execute bit; you pick the shell. chmod + ./file: execute bit; sha-bang picks the interpreter
cards.notes: Memory hook: sh/bash file = you pick the shell, no execute bit. chmod + ./file = file is a program; sha-bang picks the interpreter.
